chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from some of our companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

Regarding a man who buys a garment or goods and finds a defect in it: He said, 'If the garment is still intact (not altered), he returns it to its owner and takes back the price. But if the garment has been cut, sewn, or dyed, he returns it with a deduction for the defect.'

key_terms.قَائِمًا بِعَيْنِهِ: still intact / in its original state

ai.seo_question: What are the buyer's rights when a purchased item has a hidden defect?
ai.summary: This hadith from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *khiyar al-'ayb* (option of defect) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between full rescission when the item is intact and partial compensation (*ta'wid*) when it has been altered. It reflects the practical application of fairness in commercial transactions, ensuring the buyer is not penalized for defects they did not cause, while protecting the seller from total loss if the buyer has already utilized or modified the goods. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precise contractual obligations and the mitigation of uncertainty (*gharar*) in trade.
